questions.question: What feature of the xenograft model enabled the authors to detect regression at the micrometastatic stage?

options.A: MDA-MB-231 HM cells carried a highly sensitive codon-optimized luciferase reporter for longitudinal bioluminescence imaging
options.B: The mice expressed a fluorescent tumor suppressor that marked only large lesions
options.C: Tumors were tracked by weekly MRI without a reporter
options.D: A viral barcode was measured only after euthanasia

questions.rationale: Sensitive luciferase imaging made small metastatic foci visible before they reached advanced size.
questions.evidence_quote: This model employs a highly sensitive luciferase reporter of cancer cells, which enables the study of early-stage micro-metastases.

questions.question: At what signal threshold and primary-tumor size were tumors excised in the spontaneous-metastasis protocol?

options.A: At 10^6 photons/s, about 3–4 weeks after injection, with a mean primary tumor volume near 80 mm³
options.B: At 10^7 photons/s within 24 h, with a primary tumor near 800 mm³
options.C: At 10^5 photons/s after 50 days, with a 10-mm tumor
options.D: At 10^6 photons/s only after all lung lesions were visible by histology

questions.rationale: The intervention was timed to early metastatic burden and a measured primary-tumor size.
questions.evidence_quote: Once metastatic foci reached a total count of 10 6 photons/s (~ 3-4 weeks post injection), the primary tumor (average size of 80mm 3 ) was excised

questions.question: How did regression after primary-tumor excision depend on metastatic lesion size?

options.A: Small foci regressed markedly, whereas larger foci showed significantly less regression
options.B: Large foci regressed more strongly than small foci
options.C: Both sizes progressed identically after resection
options.D: Only established large metastases were affected by sham surgery

questions.rationale: The findings support dependence on early metastatic stage rather than a uniform response across lesion sizes.
questions.evidence_quote: To test whether regression is specific to early metastatic stages, tumors were excised from mice bearing either small (10 6 photons/sec) or large (10 7 photons/sec) metastases; regression was significantly less prominent in larger metastases

questions.question: What did the sham-surgery comparison establish about the cause of metastatic regression?

options.A: Metastases regressed after tumor excision but continued growing after sham surgery, arguing against surgery alone
options.B: Both excision and sham surgery caused equal regression
options.C: Sham surgery produced stronger regression than excision
options.D: Neither group changed, indicating the imaging signal was unstable

questions.rationale: The sham incision controls surgical trauma while leaving the primary tumor and its secretome in place.
questions.evidence_quote: Metastases regressed significantly following excision of the primary tumor, while continued to increase in mice subjected to sham surgery, p<0.05

questions.question: What happened when conditioned medium was supplied after primary-tumor excision?

options.A: Tumor-cell conditioned medium caused about tenfold less regression than serum-free medium
options.B: Conditioned medium caused tenfold greater regression than serum-free medium
options.C: Conditioned medium had no effect because the pump delivered the full tumor secretome
options.D: Serum-free medium prevented regression while conditioned medium accelerated it

questions.rationale: Partial replenishment of secretome after excision rescued metastatic foci, implicating tumor-derived soluble factors.
questions.evidence_quote: Mice that were treated with tumor-cell conditioned medium showed 10-fold less regression than mice that received serum-free medium, p<0.005 (Fig. 2D ), indicating that secreted factors from the primary tumor support survival of distant metastases.

questions.question: How much secretome delivery did the conditioned-medium pumps provide relative to the estimated intact primary tumor?

options.A: About one-eighth of the amount released daily by the primary tumor
options.B: Approximately eight times the intact tumor's daily output
options.C: An amount equal to the entire tumor's total lifetime output
options.D: No estimate was possible because pump flow was uncontrolled

questions.rationale: The authors estimate pump replacement was partial, not a full recreation of tumor secretome exposure.
questions.evidence_quote: We estimate that the amount of secreted factors released daily by the osmotic mini-pumps was ~1/8 of the amount produced daily in vivo by the primary tumor (see Methods).

questions.question: Which in vitro effects of tumor-cell conditioned medium supported a pro-metastatic secretome mechanism?

options.A: It enhanced cancer-cell viability and adhesion and induced endothelial tube formation
options.B: It increased cancer-cell apoptosis and inhibited adhesion and angiogenesis
options.C: It affected only tumor-cell proliferation, with no endothelial response
options.D: It reduced viability but increased tube formation only in serum-free controls

questions.rationale: The three assays connect conditioned medium to tumor-cell survival/attachment and a pro-angiogenic endothelial response.
questions.evidence_quote: We found that medium conditioned by MDA-MB-231 HM tumor cells, containing tumor-derived secreted factors (compared to serum-free medium), enhanced viability, p<0.001 (Fig. 2A ) and adhesion, p<0.01 (Fig. 2B ) of cancer cells, and induced tube formation of human endothelial cells, p<0.0001 (Fig. 2C ).

questions.question: How did the cytokine-array and proteomics results converge on candidate secretome mediators?

options.A: The array selected IL-8, PDGFaa, PAI-1/Serpin E1, and MIF; proteomics found 2,600 proteins, including 359 extracellular factors
options.B: The array identified only MIF, while proteomics found no extracellular proteins
options.C: Proteomics identified 28 cytokines and excluded all four array candidates
options.D: The assays found only intracellular proteins and no growth-related pathways

questions.rationale: The targeted differential screen and unbiased secretome analysis converged on four candidates among a broader pathway-rich extracellular set.
questions.evidence_quote: To complement this "narrow down" approach, we used an unbiased mass spectrometry proteomic analysis of CM and identified 2,600 proteins, 359 of which were annotated as extracellular factors by Gene Ontology (GO) analysis [25] , including the four factors identified using the cytokine array.

questions.question: What was the outcome of simultaneously neutralizing the four candidate factors while retaining the primary tumor?

options.A: The antibody cocktail completely blocked metastatic progression at the early stage
options.B: The cocktail caused immediate regression only after the primary tumor was removed
options.C: Neutralization had no effect unless each antibody was given at 100 µg
options.D: The isotype control completely blocked metastasis

questions.rationale: The intervention directly tested whether IL-8, PDGFaa, Serpin E1, and MIF together support early metastatic progression.
questions.evidence_quote: Antibody neutralization of these factors completely blocked metastatic progression, p<0.0001

questions.question: What limits the generalization of the proposed four-factor mechanism beyond the tested model?

options.A: Only the combined blockade was tested, and other tumor lines may use different or additional mediators
options.B: Each factor was independently shown to be necessary in every cancer type
options.C: The study tested multiple syngeneic tumor lines and found identical results
options.D: No in vivo neutralization was attempted

questions.rationale: The authors acknowledge that other secreted factors likely contribute and call for testing additional tumor models to assess generalizability.
questions.evidence_quote: Given the multiple factors potentially mediating the pro-metastatic effects of MDA-MB-231 HM secretome, we herein tested only the combined effect of blocking four key secreted factors known to promote malignant progression. Other secreted factors are likely to also be involved in supporting metastatic progression. Different tumors, specifically syngeneic lines, should be similarly studied to test the generalizability of the novel phenomenon observed in the current study
